diagnostic_evidence.quote: In other words, the MFCQ holds taking into account the joint dependence in \(\pvar,\param\), not just the partial dependence in \(\pvar\)
the constraint qualification holds jointly in \(\pvar,\param\), see Remark \ref{rem:jointMFCQ} and the chain rule \cite[Theorem 10.6]{rockafellar1998variational} applies to the indicators

issues.failure_explanation: The premise of (eq:mfcqduo) quantifies over all (\lambda,\mu) in R^m x R^p with sign constraints only on the active components of \lambda and no requirement that inactive multipliers vanish. As stated the implication is false: take n=q=1, m=2, no equality constraints, g_1(x,\theta)=x, g_2(x,\theta)=-x-1 at (x,\theta)=(0,0). MFCQ holds there (only g_1 is active, nabla_x g_1 = 1), but \lambda=(1,1), \mu=0 satisfies \lambda_1 nabla g_1 + \lambda_2 nabla g_2 = (1,0)+(-1,0) = 0 with \lambda_1 \ge 0, while the conclusion requires \lambda_1 = 0. The implication becomes valid only when the sum is restricted to active constraints (equivalently \lambda in the normal cone N_{R^m_-}(G(x,\theta)), i.e. \lambda \ge 0 with \lambda_i g_i(x,\theta)=0); under that restriction the x-part of the equation plus the partial MFCQ (eq:22122025b) yields the conclusion. Note the proof of Proposition prop:locboundp uses exactly this active-index reduction via complementarity, confirming that the unrestricted version is not what can be justified.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the premise of (eq:mfcqduo) with the sum over i in I(x,\theta) only (as in (eq:22122025b)) or, equivalently, require \lambda_i = 0 for inactive i (\lambda in N_{R^m_-}(G(x,\theta))); the x-component of the joint equation together with the partial MFCQ then gives the conclusion.
issues.overall_effect: The joint-MFCQ implication (eq:mfcqduo) is false as written. It is cited in Section 4.2 to justify applying the chain rule [Theorem 10.6, Rockafellar-Wets] jointly in (x,\theta) when deriving (eq:clarkesubdiffvf); the qualification actually needed there is the active-support (normal-cone) version, so that derivation is restored by the same fix, and (eq:clarkesubdiffvf) is in any case implied independently by Theorem theo:main.
issues.title: Joint MFCQ implication in Remark rem:jointMFCQ is false as stated
issues.why_classification: A one-line, standard correction of the premise; the intended joint qualification then holds and its only downstream use (the chain rule in Section 4.2) is valid, so no claim, method, or scope is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof defines D_L(y,\theta) with D_F(x,\theta) (no convex hull), but the theorem's D_f, the KKT map Mult, and Lemma lem:edlem9 all use conv D_F. Two steps break as written. (i) For (x,\lambda,\mu) in Sol_pd(\theta), stationarity only gives 0 in conv D_{F(.,\theta)}(x) + jac_xG^T\lambda + jac_xH^T\mu, i.e. the multiplier term lies in the convex hull of the x-projection of D_F; since conservative fields may have nonconvex values (e.g. D(0)={0,1} is conservative for x -> max(x,0)), the fiber {u : (0,u) in D_L(x,\lambda,\mu,\theta)} can be empty, making (eq:uzeroarb) vacuous. (ii) The closing identity identifies D_f(\theta(t)) with cl Union_\ell {u : (0,u) in D_L(y_\ell(t),\theta(t))} by quoting Lemma lem:edlem9, but that lemma is stated with conv D_F, so the identity is unjustified for the proof's D_L.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define D_L(y,\theta) := conv D_F(x,\theta) + (jac_xG^T\lambda + jac_xH^T\mu, jac_\theta G^T\lambda + jac_\theta H^T\mu) and add the one-line observation that conv D_F is again a (definable) conservative field for F: the chain rule in Definition def:conservative holds for all field values simultaneously at almost every t, hence extends to convex combinations. All remaining steps are unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the proof of Theorem theo:main does not establish the chain rule for the convexified field D_f of the theorem statement: (eq:uzeroarb) may be vacuous and the final density identity misquotes Lemma lem:edlem9. Theorem theo:mainsmooth, proved as a special case of Theorem theo:main, and its consequences in Remark rmk:consequenceasm inherit the gap until repaired.
issues.title: Convex hull missing from the set-valued map D_L defined in the proof of Theorem theo:main
issues.why_classification: Forced local correction (insert the convex hull already present in the theorem statement and in Lemma lem:edlem9) plus a routine one-line fact; the statement, the method, and all consequences survive unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let \(\varphi\colon \Rell \to \R\) be a locally Lipschitz function and \(\consv_{\varphi}\colon \Rell \to \Rell\) be a locally bounded and graph closed set-valued map with nonempty values.
The value function \(f\), defined in \eqref{eq:fvdef}, is continuous on \(\Rq\).

issues.failure_explanation: Per Definition def:conservative, the conclusion 'D_f is a conservative field for f' is defined only for locally Lipschitz f, and the cited reduction [Theorem 2, pauwels2023conservative] is what upgrades the verified chain rule along C^1 definable curves to that conclusion. The paper never proves f locally Lipschitz: Lemma lem:fcont establishes only continuity, which is strictly weaker even for definable data (\theta -> sqrt(|\theta|) is semialgebraic and continuous but not Lipschitz at 0). Thus a hypothesis required by the definition of the conclusion, and by the invoked reduction, is used without being established. The missing fact is true under Assumptions ass:standing: the proof of Lemma lem:rinnersemicontinuous shows the feasible map R has the Aubin property around every feasible point, which combined with the local boundedness of Sol_p (ass:a3) and the local Lipschitz continuity of F yields the standard estimate |f(\theta_1)-f(\theta_2)| \le L(1+\kappa)||\theta_1-\theta_2|| locally.

failure_location.quote: According to \cite[Theorem 2 and Lemma 6]{pauwels2023conservative}, to finish the proof, it remains to show that \(\consv_f\) has the chain rule property along continuously differentiable  and definable curves.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the standard lemma that f is locally Lipschitz under Assumptions ass:standing: for \theta_1,\theta_2 near \bar\theta and x_1 in Sol_p(\theta_1), the Aubin property of R (uniformized over the compact set of nearby minimizers) gives \tilde x_2 in R(\theta_2) with ||\tilde x_2 - x_1|| \le \kappa||\theta_1-\theta_2||, hence f(\theta_2)-f(\theta_1) \le F(\tilde x_2,\theta_2)-F(x_1,\theta_1) \le L(1+\kappa)||\theta_1-\theta_2||, and symmetrically.
issues.overall_effect: The conclusion of Theorem theo:main is not fully established as stated; Theorem theo:mainsmooth and the consequences drawn in Remark rmk:consequenceasm (notably item (iv), which applies Clarke's Lipschitz calculus to f) share the same gap.
issues.title: Local Lipschitz continuity of the value function f is used but never established
issues.why_classification: The gap is filled by a short, standard sensitivity estimate built entirely from facts already in the paper (the Aubin property shown inside Lemma lem:rinnersemicontinuous's proof, local boundedness of Sol_p, local Lipschitz F); no claim, guarantee, or scope is weakened.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Moreover  \(\bar{g}\) is differentiable and locally Lipschitz on \(\Rell\).

issues.failure_explanation: The balls must avoid C (otherwise the positive bump forces \bar g > 0 at a point of C), so r_k < dist(z_k,C); but the stated conditions still allow e.g. r_k = dist(z_k,C)/3, for which \bar g need not be differentiable at points of C. Concretely, C = {0} in R, z_k = 2^{-k}, r_k = 2^{-k}/3 satisfy r_k > 0, r_k -> 0, pairwise disjoint balls avoiding C, and the difference quotient of \bar g at 0 along h_k = z_k equals \bar f(z_k)/z_k + \varphi(0) r_k/z_k -> \varphi(0)/3 \neq 0 (since \bar f is smooth with \bar f(0)=0, nabla \bar f(0)=0), while it tends to 0 along h_k = -z_k; hence \bar g is not differentiable at 0 in C. Differentiability on C is essential to the claim and to item (ii) of Claim theo:counterex. The missing requirement is r_k = o(dist(z_k,C)): with e.g. r_k \le dist(z_k,C)^2, any z+h in a ball obeys ||h|| \ge dist(z_k,C) - r_k \ge dist(z_k,C)/2 and the bump term is at most \varphi_max r_k \le 4 \varphi_max ||h||^2 = o(||h||), giving nabla \bar g = 0 on C.

failure_location.quote: For any \(k \in \N\), consider \(\Bcal(z_k,r_k)\) such that \(r_k > 0\), \(r_k \xrightarrow[k \to \infny]{} 0\), and \(\Bcal(z_k,r_k) \cap \Bcal(z_{s},r_{s}) = \varnothing\) for \(s \neq k\).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the smallness condition r_k \le dist(z_k,C)^2 (compatible with disjointness and r_k -> 0 since z_k not in C and z_k is not an accumulation point of the sequence) and the two-line estimate \bar g(z+h) = o(||h||) for z in C; every other step is unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The constructed function is not shown to be differentiable at points of C, so Claim lem:fnctcounterex is unproven as written; Claim theo:counterex, which builds its objective F from this construction and asserts differentiability on all of R^2, inherits the gap (its conclusion is restored once the radii are shrunk).
issues.title: Bump radii in Claim lem:fnctcounterex do not ensure differentiability on C
issues.why_classification: A local strengthening of the radius choice plus a routine estimate repairs the construction; the claimed function then has all stated properties, and the counterexample and all downstream conclusions survive.
